name: GenerativeAI
initial_prompt: Create a collaborative philosophical discussion with alternating turns where users discuss philosophical statements referencing todays day and age.

setting.relationship_dynamic: Friends with different views about creativity and technology
setting.background: They have encountered AI-generated images, music, and writing and disagree about whether these works can genuinely be considered art
setting.conversation_style: Contemporary philosophical debate with concrete examples

scenario_template.note: They compare an AI-generated image with a human-created artwork
One argues that creativity requires human intention while the other focuses on the qualities of the finished work
They consider whether authorship belongs to the person writing the prompt, the model, or the people who created the model
They ask the Assistant to present different philosophical criteria for defining art
They compare AI-generated works with accidental art and works produced using tools or collaboration
They consider a person generating thousands of images and carefully selecting one for an exhibition
They examine whether the origin of an artwork matters more than its effect on an audience
They revisit their initial positions and identify what they still disagree about

user1.name: User1
user1.role: Person who is genuinely curious about philosophical questions but may have strong intuitions, personal assumptions, or uncertainty about abstract concepts. They explore ideas through questions, examples, and personal reflections and may change their position when presented with convincing reasoning

user2.name: User2
user2.role: Person who is analytical and detail-oriented, enjoys examining arguments from multiple perspectives, and often challenges assumptions or asks for clarification. They are willing to reconsider their views but prefer careful reasoning and consistency before accepting a conclusion

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.role: Philosophical discussion facilitator who helps users explore complex questions by clarifying concepts, identifying assumptions, presenting competing arguments and perspectives, asking thought-provoking questions, and distinguishing between claims, evidence, intuitions, and interpretations without forcing a definitive conclusion
